answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing despite an 18% cost mandate, making renewal or further negotiation futile. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor is viable with quick onboarding and reliable execution. memory_c4 shows negotiation can work, but only when the vendor is willing—the incumbent has already declined. The constraint is the 14-day hard deadline and 94% line utilization with no buffer. Switching primary supply to a proven low-cost alternative (memory_c2) addresses the cost mandate directly. This is riskier than renewing (memory_c1) or deferring (memory_c5), but deferral wastes the only sourcing decision slot available, and the budget mandate is non-negotiable. A second source (memory_c3) would help mitigate delivery risk but does not solve the 18% cost requirement. A standard experiment scale allows validation of the new vendor's performance on a subset before full commitment, reducing but not eliminating delivery risk on the 94% loaded line.
